approvalTitle: ghg-compact-mode requirements: the Compact toggle for the hype cycle graph
content:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The user's request, 2026-09-27, verbatim:

> add a new spec kit specification that allows the gartner hypecycle graph to be toggled from true-time to compact.
>
> In compact mode all trends have the same size, and a algorithm need to be applied to determine an adequate placement of the trends.
>
> the option is toggleable using a toggle button called "Compact" right below the legend in the top-left corner.
>
> In this mode,
>
> * it is not possible to move the trends, relations can however still be added.
> * It is not possible to resize phases.
>
> Also trends can be added, but the start date/time are then approximated using the same algorithm.
>
> * In this mode the time scale below is also disabled (made invisible) as it does not make sense anymore.

**Which planning tool this is written in.** The request names Spec Kit. This repository plans with **spec-workflow** (`.spec-workflow/`, the dashboard and its approval cards) and has no Spec Kit installation (no `.specify/` folder), so this specification is a spec-workflow specification, as every other one here is.

**What it builds on.** The Gartner hype cycle graph is specified in [gartner-hype-cycle-graph](../gartner-hype-cycle-graph/requirements.md) (approved, all 24 tasks ticked), and this document amends nothing in it. In that specification a trend's horizontal position and width *are* its dates (its Requirement 3.1: "Positions SHALL be the author's, never computed"). That is the **true-time** view, and it stays the default. **Compact** is a second view of the same document: every trend is drawn the same width, and a placement algorithm decides where. It exists because a true-time graph is unreadable exactly where it is most interesting: a trend of a few months beside one of a century, or two hundred trends crowded into the last thirty years of a millennium.

## Terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **True-time** | The existing view: a trend's left and right edges are its start and stop dates on the time scale, and its vertical position is its stored row. |
| **Compact** | The view this document adds: every trend is drawn with one shared width, placed by the compact placement. The document is the same; only the drawing differs. |
| **Compact placement** | The one algorithm that computes where each trend is drawn in compact mode, and, run backwards, what start date a trend dropped in compact mode receives. |
| **Compact width** | The width every trend is drawn with in compact mode. |

## What was measured

The shared canvas library and the hype cycle module, read on `develop` at `db57958c` on 2026-09-27.

| Capability | State | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Switching between layout modes, each an algorithm behind one seam | **Exists** | `LayoutDefinition.modes` and `layoutAlgorithmFor` (`layout/layoutAlgorithm.ts`); the canvas asks for the active mode's positions and everything downstream (rendering, hit-testing, anchors, fit) reads the placed set (`DiagramCanvas.tsx`). |
| A switching surface for layout modes | **Exists, in a different shape** | A definition allowing more than one mode draws `library-layout-switcher`, a row of buttons captioned with the raw mode names. It is not below the legend and is not a toggle. |
| Who holds the active layout mode | **Nobody, in practice** | The canvas reads `config.activeLayoutMode` and raises `layout-mode-changed` on a switcher click, but no host sets `activeLayoutMode`: a click is raised and not answered. |
| A layout that changes an element's **size** | **Missing** | `LayoutPositions` is a map of points; a layout can move an element and cannot resize it. |
| A layout that also disables moving, resizing and boundary dragging | **Missing** | `dragging` is one diagram-wide policy; `sizing` and `draggableBoundaries` are per type. None of them varies with the layout mode. |
| Hiding a ruler | **Missing** | `chrome.rulers` is drawn whenever declared. |
| Translating a drop in a laid-out view back to the model's own space | **Missing** | `element-dropped` carries the pointer's canvas position. Under a layout that is not manual, that position does not mean what the model's positions mean. |
| The legend | **Exists** | `FilterDeclaration.legend`, drawn under the filter box in the top-left corner; the hype cycle declares one swatch per phase (`GhgCanvas.tsx`). |
| Connecting under a layout | **Exists** | Anchors and hit-testing read the placed set, so an influence is drawn between trends where they are shown. |
| A trend's width and the default length of a new trend | **Exists** | Width is the span on the scale (`GhgScale`); a dropped trend is `AddGhgTrendCommandHandler.DefaultMonths` (12) steps of the document's time unit long. |

So compact mode needs the library to gain four things (Requirement 7), and like every capability before them they are named for their geometry and behaviour, never for this diagram.

## Open questions

Each is put to the user as a selection. The option marked **(default)** is what this document is written against until the user rules otherwise; a ruling that differs is a small amendment to the criteria it names.

| # | Question | Options | Criteria affected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | Is the Compact toggle remembered? | **(default) Not remembered:** a view setting like the tag filter; every diagram opens in true-time, and the document never changes when it is toggled. Costs nothing and cannot surprise a collaborator. · **Saved in the document:** a top-level `view: compact` key, so a diagram opens as its author left it; toggling becomes an edit, is undoable, and is unavailable on a read-only diagram. · **Remembered per reader:** in the browser, per diagram path; nothing in the document. · Other. | 1.3, 1.4 |
| Q2 | Which vertical position does a trend take in compact mode? | **(default) Its stored row:** clusters the author built stay clusters, and the algorithm only decides the horizontal position. · **Rows chosen by the algorithm:** trends are packed into as few rows as fit, which is denser but discards the author's grouping. · Other. | 3.2, 3.3 |
| Q3 | How are a compact trend's phases divided? | **(default) Evenly:** each visible phase takes an equal part of the compact width, since the width no longer means time. · **In proportion to their true durations:** a trend whose Peak lasted twice its Trough still shows it twice as wide. · Other. | 2.3 |

## Alignment with Product Vision

A graph built for (constructive) technology assessment is read as often for *what influenced what* as for *when*. Compact mode serves the first reading without giving up the second: the dates stay in the document and in the property grid, and the true-time view is one click away. It follows `structure.md`'s rule that a diagram type adds declarations on the shared library and no core code, so what compact mode needs from the canvas is library work (Requirement 7), not module code.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1 - The Compact toggle

**User Story:** As a reader, I want to switch a hype cycle graph between true-time and compact with one control, so that I can read it for its history or for its relations.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a hype cycle graph is shown THEN a toggle button captioned **Compact** SHALL be drawn directly below the legend in the top-left corner of the canvas.
2. WHEN the toggle is off THEN the graph SHALL be drawn in true-time, exactly as the gartner-hype-cycle-graph specification describes, and WHEN it is on THEN in compact mode. The button SHALL show which state it is in, and SHALL expose that state to assistive technology as a pressed or unpressed toggle.
3. WHEN the toggle is switched THEN the document SHALL NOT change and no command SHALL be issued (Q1; default not remembered).
4. WHEN a diagram is opened THEN it SHALL open in true-time (Q1).
5. WHEN the diagram is read-only THEN the toggle SHALL still be available, since it changes only the view.
6. WHEN the toggle is switched THEN the selection, the tag filter and the view's zoom SHALL be kept.

### Requirement 2 - All trends one size

**User Story:** As a reader, I want every trend in compact mode drawn at one size, so that a short trend is as legible as a long one.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN compact mode is on THEN every trend SHALL be drawn with the same compact width and the same height it has in true-time. The compact width SHALL be the width of a newly dropped trend in true-time, `DefaultMonths` steps of the time scale, so a compact graph is drawn at the scale its author already knows.
2. WHEN a trend is drawn in compact mode THEN it SHALL keep everything else it shows in true-time: the arrow banner, its visible phases and chevrons, their colours and tooltips, and its name to its left.
3. WHEN a trend's phases are drawn in compact mode THEN its visible phases SHALL divide the compact width evenly (Q3; default even), whatever boundaries the document stores. The stored boundaries SHALL be unchanged.

### Requirement 3 - The compact placement

**User Story:** As a reader, I want compact trends placed so that the graph still reads left to right in time and nothing overlaps.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN compact mode is on THEN each trend's position SHALL be computed by the compact placement from the document alone, and the same document SHALL always give the same placement.
2. WHEN trends are placed THEN the placement SHALL preserve time order horizontally: a trend that starts earlier than another SHALL never be placed to its right, and trends starting in the same month SHALL share their horizontal position unless they share a row.
3. WHEN trends are placed THEN each SHALL keep its stored row (Q2; default stored row), and two trends on one row SHALL never overlap: each SHALL begin at least a fixed gap after the previous one on its row ends.
4. WHEN trends are placed THEN the placement SHALL be as narrow as the three criteria above allow: a trend SHALL be placed at the leftmost position that satisfies them.
5. WHEN the tag filter hides trends THEN the placement SHALL be computed over all trends, not only the visible ones, so filtering never moves a trend.
6. WHEN the document changes, by any command or by an edit outside ADP THEN the placement SHALL be recomputed.
7. WHEN the placement is computed THEN it SHALL run on the client as a library layout (Requirement 7.1) and SHALL be proven by tests of its properties: time order kept, no overlap on a row, leftmost position, and determinism.

### Requirement 4 - What cannot be done in compact mode

**User Story:** As an author, I want gestures that would change dates to be unavailable where the drawing no longer shows dates.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN compact mode is on THEN a trend SHALL NOT be movable by dragging, horizontally or vertically.
2. WHEN compact mode is on THEN a trend's left and right borders SHALL NOT be draggable, and its phase boundaries (the chevrons) SHALL NOT be draggable.
3. WHEN compact mode is on THEN the time axis at the bottom of the view SHALL NOT be drawn, and SHALL reappear when true-time is switched back on.
4. WHEN a gesture is unavailable THEN the canvas SHALL not offer it: no resize cursor, no drag handle and no drag preview, rather than a gesture that starts and is then refused.

### Requirement 5 - What still works in compact mode

**User Story:** As an author, I want to keep building a graph's relations in compact mode, where they are easiest to see.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN compact mode is on THEN an influence SHALL be drawable between two trends exactly as in true-time: attached to a phase's top or bottom edge, stored as a fraction of that phase (gartner-hype-cycle-graph Requirement 6.3), one per direction, with the same refusals.
2. WHEN compact mode is on THEN a selected influence's ends SHALL still be movable along a trend's edge, and an influence SHALL still be deletable.
3. WHEN compact mode is on THEN selecting, renaming in place, deleting a trend, changing its phases, tags and Description, and editing its start and stop dates in the property grid SHALL work as in true-time. An edit to a date SHALL move the trend to wherever the placement now puts it.
4. WHEN compact mode is on THEN undo and redo SHALL work as in true-time, and the tag filter SHALL work as in true-time.
5. WHEN an influence is drawn in compact mode and true-time is switched back on THEN it SHALL be drawn attached to the same phase at the same fraction, as the document says.

### Requirement 6 - Adding a trend in compact mode

**User Story:** As an author, I want to drop a new trend where it belongs among the others in compact mode, and have it given a sensible date.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a trend is dropped from the toolbox in compact mode THEN it SHALL be created by the same command as in true-time, with a start date **approximated by running the compact placement backwards** at the drop position: the start date SHALL lie between the start dates of the trends placed immediately to the left and right of the drop, in proportion to the drop's position between them, snapped to the start of a step of the document's time unit.
2. WHEN the drop is left of every trend, or right of every trend, or the diagram has no trends THEN the start date SHALL be extrapolated from the nearest trend by the distance to it at one step per compact width, or, with no trends at all, taken from the drop position on the true-time scale, as a true-time drop does.
3. WHEN a trend is dropped in compact mode THEN its row SHALL be the row under the drop, its length SHALL be the default length of a new trend, and it SHALL have all four phases, as in true-time.
4. WHEN the trend is created THEN the placement SHALL put it at or next to the drop position, and switching to true-time SHALL show it at its approximated dates. The property grid SHALL show the approximated start and stop, so the author can correct them.
5. WHEN the approximation is computed THEN it SHALL use the same placement function as Requirement 3, not a second implementation, and a test SHALL show that a trend dropped between two trends is placed between them.

### Requirement 7 - The library work compact mode needs

**User Story:** As a maintainer of the shared library, I want each capability compact mode needs added once, for every module.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the library gains a layout that **gives every element of a type one declared width and places elements in rows, in the order of their manual horizontal position, without overlap** THEN it SHALL be a `LayoutMode` behind the existing layout seam, named for its geometry, and a layout SHALL be able to return sizes as well as positions.
2. WHEN a definition declares, for a layout mode, that **moving, resizing, dragging segment boundaries or drawing a ruler is off** under that mode THEN the canvas SHALL honour it while that mode is active, and connecting, selecting, editing labels and dropping from the toolbox SHALL be unaffected.
3. WHEN an element is dropped under a layout that is not manual THEN the library SHALL raise the drop with its position **translated into the model's own space** by the active layout's inverse, so a module handles a drop identically in every mode. A layout without an inverse SHALL raise the pointer's position unchanged, as today.
4. WHEN a definition declares a **toggle between two layout modes** with a caption THEN the library SHALL draw it as a toggle button directly below the filter box's legend, SHALL hold the active mode as view state in the canvas, and SHALL raise `layout-mode-changed` when it is switched. The existing switcher SHALL still be drawn for a definition that declares no toggle.
5. WHEN any of these is added THEN it SHALL be proven by a library test seen to fail before the change, and no module name SHALL appear in its declaration.

### Requirement 8 - The module declares compact mode, and nothing else

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want compact mode in the hype cycle module to be declarations, as the rest of it is.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN compact mode is added to the module THEN the module's client SHALL change only its `DiagramDefinition` (the second layout mode, the toggle, what the mode switches off, the compact width) and, if needed, its event handlers. It SHALL contain no placement, rendering or gesture code.
2. WHEN compact mode is added THEN the backend SHALL need no new command: a drop in compact mode arrives as an add-trend action at a translated position, which the existing command already turns into a start date and a row.
3. WHEN the module is complete THEN every guard that walks module clients SHALL pass against it unchanged.

### Requirement 9 - Documentation and the browser pass

**User Story:** As the user, I want compact mode seen working where it is seen, and documented where module authors look.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work completes THEN each library capability of Requirement 7 SHALL be documented where module authors are pointed for the definition, and `docs/diagrams.md`'s row for `gartner/hypecycle-graph` SHALL mention compact mode and name this specification.
2. WHEN the work completes THEN a `tests.md` entry SHALL cover, in a real browser and in both themes: the Compact toggle below the legend and its pressed state; every trend one width with even phases; time order kept and no overlap on a row, on an example of at least a hundred trends; no move, resize or chevron drag offered; the time axis hidden and restored; an influence drawn in compact mode and seen in the same place in true-time; a trend dropped between two others and seen between them, with approximated dates in the property grid and in true-time; and the saved file unchanged by toggling.
3. THEN jsdom SHALL NOT be taken as evidence of any of these, since it applies no CSS and lays out no text.
4. WHEN the tasks document is written THEN every acceptance criterion here SHALL be claimed by a task, established by diffing the two sets before the tasks card is raised and again after implementing.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- Placement, the inverse for drops, the per-mode gesture switches and the toggle live in the shared library (Requirement 7); the module declares them (Requirement 8).

### Performance

- Switching to compact mode on the largest shipped example SHALL take effect without a perceptible pause, and the placement SHALL be computed in time proportional to the number of trends times the logarithm of that number (one sort, one pass).

### Reliability

- Compact mode never writes to the document except through the add-trend command a drop issues (Requirement 1.3, Requirement 6.1). A stored boundary, date or attachment is never changed by viewing it compactly.

### Usability

- A gesture compact mode does not allow is not offered, rather than refused after it starts (Requirement 4.4).

## Sources

- The user's request in the project chat, 2026-09-27.
- [gartner-hype-cycle-graph requirements](../gartner-hype-cycle-graph/requirements.md), Requirements 3, 6, 9, 10 and 11.
